sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and imports
sections.what: Loads the standard tools for handling file paths and type labels.
sections.why: Likely reason: file lookup needs these tools. No other reason is stated in the code.

sections.name: TemplateSelector (part 1)
sections.title: Trying exact proposal file names
sections.what: Takes the RFP file name, works out its base name, and builds five likely proposal file names to try in order.
sections.why: Likely reason: the naming convention is known, so exact names are tried before any looser search.
sections.watch_out: Only the proposals folder is searched, so a proposal stored anywhere else will not be found.

sections.name: TemplateSelector (part 2)
sections.title: Returning the match or the failure
sections.what: Returns the first exact file found. If none exists, it runs the looser search. If that also fails, it lists the available proposals and returns nothing. It also removes the file extension and RFP-style suffixes to form the base name.
sections.why: Likely reason: trying the most exact match first avoids picking a wrong file.
sections.watch_out: Suffix removal only matches the listed spellings, so an unusual RFP name may keep extra words.

sections.name: TemplateSelector (part 3)
sections.title: Looser search and file listing
sections.what: Searches the proposal folder for any deck whose name contains the base name, ignoring case, and returns the first one found. It also provides a sorted list of all proposal files.
sections.why: Likely reason: file names are not always exact, so a name-contains check catches close matches.
sections.watch_out: Short base names match many files, and the first match depends on the order the operating system lists files.

summary: Finds the proposal template file that matches a matched RFP by comparing file names.
purpose: Choose the right example proposal deck for each RFP.
why: The docstring states the convention: a file named ProjectName_RFP is matched to ProjectName_Proposal. The code does not say why the looser search is also included.
how: Remove the file extension and any RFP-style suffix to get a base name. Try five likely proposal file names in order. If none exists, search the proposal folder for any deck whose name contains the base name. If nothing matches, print the proposal files available and return nothing.
inputs: The matched RFP file name, and the proposals folder, which defaults to data/proposals relative to where the program runs.
outputs: The path to the matching proposal file as text, or nothing when no match exists. A separate function returns a sorted list of all proposal paths.
risks: A very short base name can match many files. The looser search returns the first file found, and the order of files depends on the operating system. A base name that is empty matches every file. The default folder is relative, so the program can find nothing if run from another folder.
debug: Turn on verbose output and check the printed base name. Confirm the expected file exists in data/proposals with the exact spelling. Read the list of available proposals printed on failure. If the wrong deck is picked, the looser search is the likely cause.
